parsed.explanation: No traveller-facing exposure is documented: gender expression is lawful, self-determination legal recognition with an X marker exists, bathroom access is protected, and anti-discrimination plus hate-crime law covers gender identity, backed by an official equality complaints body and published hate-crime reporting routes — functioning visitor-facing protections of the 0.85–0.95 tier. Social acceptance is directly evidenced: large pride turnout, a head of state attending pride, settled relationship law, conversion-therapy ban. Deductions: police-recorded potential hate crimes are small but rising (16 in 2023), not disaggregated to trans people; acknowledged protection gaps are unspecified; outlying-area attitudes toward trans people specifically are unevidenced (thin data, not documented hostility); the strong index ranking measures gay/lesbian conditions only. No universal exclusion, no organised targeting, no custody or border friction documented.
